messages.text:
"I want to make a top down 3rd person RPG. The concept is a frustrated father raising 3 daughters. The girls are smart yet unruly and witting. The father has to accomplish household chores and attempt to get the 3 girls to help. He has to use his own wit and cleverness to get the girls to do chores. There is also a great pyrenees named Charlie who appears at times and adds to the chaos. he has the personality of a sterotypical great pyrenees. the girls names are Elaina, who is 12, elsie who is 9, and ellerie who is 5. The game starts in the morning with father in bed and the girls getting up at different times and waking up. he has to feed them, or convince them to work together to make breakfast for them selves. some of the tasks that need done are showers, doing laundry and dishes, etc. The day progresses to getting everyone in bed at night and everyone asleep. You win the game when everyone is asleep. Some things to take into consideration are everyones focus, and dad needs mental health breaks occassonally without losing his temper. If dad loses his temper too many times you lose the game. There should be on screen controls with buttons and arrows to move the dad around. The children characters on screen move on their own according to whatever each characters agenda is. the house should have 2 bedrooms. the girls all share one bedroom, the father has one bedroom. there is a bathroom with washer and dryer in it, and a kitchen and a living room. there are various distractions for the girls such as toys, tv, books and sometimes escaping outside. the girls also need breaks occasionally where they are allowed a distraction in order to stay on task.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete playable top-down third-person RPG about a frustrated father managing three daughters, chores, distractions, and household chaos.

## Requirements
- Start in the father’s bed in the morning.
- Include Elaina (12), Elsie (9), Ellerle (5), and Charlie the Great Pyrenees.
- Include two bedrooms, bathroom with washer/dryer, kitchen, living room, and door passages between rooms.
- Provide chores such as breakfast, showers, laundry, dishes, and bedtime.
- Add autonomous child agendas and distractions: toys, TV, books, and escaping outside.
- Track focus and dad mental health; too much temper loss loses the game.
- Winning condition is everyone asleep in bed.
- Add visible on-screen movement controls and D-pad-style arrows for tablets and phones.
- Keep the entire playable screen within a horizontal tablet viewport without scrolling.
- Ensure the dad can escape from the bedroom and move throughout the house.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a single-page browser game with a top-down illustrated house scene.
- Added a responsive canvas layout, sidebar dashboard, touch controls, character movement, room interactions, chores, timers, stats, win/loss states, and restart functionality.
- Added clickable/touch room passage areas and keyboard movement support.

## Work State
### Completed
- Complete playable game concept and implementation were requested.
- Initial HTML/CSS/JavaScript game build was created.
- Gameplay, characters, tasks, distractions, movement controls, stats, and win/loss logic were added.
- Responsive tablet-oriented layout was requested as a correction.
- Door passage support between rooms was requested as a correction.

### Active
- Ensuring the latest implementation fully displays the entire playable area in horizontal tablet orientation.
- Verifying that door passages and room boundaries no longer trap the father in the bedroom.

### Blocked
- [none]

## Next Move
1. Open `index.html` in the deployed browser and verify it renders a fully playable horizontal layout.
2. Test all door passages by moving the father from the bedroom into the hallway and adjacent rooms.
3. Verify touch D-pad and keyboard controls, chores, win/loss conditions, and tablet viewport fit.
4. Capture a screenshot for visual confirmation.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main and likely only browser game implementation.

## Important Context
- The father must be able to leave the bedroom from the start; bedroom exits and room doorways must remain passable.
- The playable area must fit within the tablet viewport horizontally with no page scrolling.

README.md
## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete playable, tablet-friendly top-down RPG about Dad managing household chores and the daily routines of Elaina, Elsie, Ellerle, and Charlie.

## Requirements
- Dad starts asleep in bed and is awakened by the kids for breakfast.
- Include two bedrooms, bathroom/laundry, kitchen, living room, hallway, outdoor exit, and passable doorways.
- Implement ordered chores in sequence: breakfast, showers, laundry, dishes, and bedtime.
- Children must move autonomously rather than teleporting.
- Age-appropriate behavior and moods for each child.
- Dad needs delegation and text-RPG interaction capabilities.
- Interactions must pause gameplay and offer parenting approaches such as calm discipline, authoritarian discipline, and bribery.
- A child’s cooperation or resistance depends on age, mood, and prior treatment.
- Parenting styles affect mood and future behavior.
- Cooperative children improve Dad’s temper; resistance lowers it.
- Dad can take a break to restore his temper.
- Keep movement controls usable by keyboard and touch.
- Preserve the winning condition of everyone asleep, and Dad losing if temper reaches zero.

## Decisions
- Use a single-page canvas game with a responsive sidebar and horizontal tablet layout.
- Use real wall segments with explicit gaps for passable doorways rather than teleporting room transitions.
- Implement interaction sequences as pausable text-based choice dialogs.
- Add visible door passages and touch D-pad controls.
- Treat chores as a strict ordered checklist rather than independently completable tasks.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the main playable implementation in `index.html`.
- Added responsive canvas, dashboard, stats, touch controls, keyboard controls, and restart functionality.
- Added the house layout, rooms, furniture, chores, distractors, characters, and win/loss logic.
- Added explicit passable door gaps so Dad can leave the bedroom and traverse the house.
- Added an initial interaction-dialog CSS layer to the page.
- Verified JavaScript syntax and captured a browser screenshot.

### Active
- Implementing the requested awake-at-breakfast opening sequence and child wake-up behavior.
- Replacing instant character repositioning with continuous, collision-aware child movement.
- Adding ordered chore enforcement and the parenting interaction system.
- Adding delegation, pauseable text RPG dialogs, discipline choices, moods, and future-behavior responses.
- Adding cooperative/resistant temper outcomes and a temper-restoring break action.

### Blocked
- Interactive browser verification is limited because Playwright’s Chromium browser executable is not installed; system Chromium was available for a screenshot instead.

## Next Move
1. Modify `index.html` so Dad begins lying in bed and Elaina, Elsie, and Ellerle walk toward him and wake him for breakfast.
2. Replace the periodic character teleport logic with targets and smooth continuous movement.
3. Enforce the current task in chore order and prevent skipping unfinished chores.
4. Add pauseable text RPG dialogs for choosing calm discipline, authoritarian discipline, bribery, delegation, or other age-appropriate approaches.
5. Track each child’s mood, temperament, and history, then calculate cooperation and temper changes accordingly.
6. Add a Dad-break station/action that restores temper and affects focus.
7. Verify room movement, child movement, ordered chores, interactions, win/loss behavior, and tablet viewport fit.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main and only browser-game implementation.

## Important Context
- Dad should not only act manually; the player needs to assign chores and resolve child behavior through dialogue choices.
- Interaction dialogs must freeze game simulation, not merely cover it visually.
- The opening sequence supersedes the prior start behavior: Dad begins in bed rather than roaming freely.
- The previous checkpoint established that the Dad must be able to exit the bedroom through open door passages; those exits remain required.
- The existing implementation includes a bed for Dad and all required characters and stations, but many of the new behavioral systems remain to be integrated.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete playable, tablet-friendly single-page top-down RPG where Dad manages breakfast and ordered household chores for Elaina, Elsie, Ellerle, and Charlie.

## Requirements
- Dad starts lying in bed and is awakened by the children, who walk toward him smoothly.
- Include two bedrooms, bathroom/laundry, kitchen, living room, hallway, outdoor exit, and passable doorways.
- Complete chores strictly in order: breakfast, showers, laundry, dishes, then bedtime.
- Children move autonomously with collision-aware, continuous movement.
- Implement age-appropriate child moods and reactions.
- Provide Dad delegation and text-RPG interactions.
- Interactions must fully pause gameplay and offer calm discipline, authoritarian discipline, bribery, and delegation.
- Cooperation or resistance depends on age, mood, style, and prior treatment.
- Cooperative children improve Dad’s temper; resistance lowers it.
- Dad can take a break to restore temper and focus.
- Preserve keyboard/touch movement and winning/losing conditions.

## Decisions
- Use a single-page canvas implementation with a responsive sidebar and tablet layout.
- Use real wall segments with explicit passable door gaps.
- Use pausable choice dialogs rather than purely visual overlays.
- Replace teleport-based child movement with target-based smooth movement.
- Keep chores enforced as an ordered checklist.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the playable `index.html` canvas game with house layout, furniture, stations, HUD, touch controls, keyboard controls, and restart.
- Added passable room doors and exterior path.
- Added Dad and child characters, stats, checklist, distraction, laundry timer, win/loss logic, and responsive sidebar.
- Added Dad-in-bed state and initial continuous waking sequence for Elaina, Elsie, and Ellerle.
- Added pause dialog markup and dialog styling.
- Added ordered chore state and task-order enforcement.
- Added delegation and parenting-style response functions.
- Added mood, age, history, cooperation/resistance, temper, focus, and break UI behavior.
- Added continuous later target movement for children.
- Verified JavaScript syntax with `new Function(...)`.

### Active
- Finish integrating and debugging the full opening sequence, dialog flow, and delegation behavior.
- Verify continuous child movement and ordered-task interactions in a browser.
- Verify Dad-break behavior and temper/focus restoration.
- Verify responsive tablet viewport behavior.

### Blocked
- Interactive browser verification remains limited because Playwright Chromium is unavailable.

## Next Move
1. Remove or correct any remaining incompatible or unfinished functions in `index.html`.
2. Verify that the opening dialog pauses all simulation until Dad gets out of bed.
3. Verify chores cannot be started out of sequence.
4. Verify mood/style outcomes, delegation, temper changes, and child mood updates.
5. Verify laundry remains an ordered timed step and dishes follow it.
6. Verify bedtime sequence and final win condition.
7. Verify dad break restores stats and pausing freezes movement.
8. Run browser/tablet viewport verification when Chromium or Playwright becomes available.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main and only browser-game implementation.

## Important Context
- The existing implementation still needs end-to-end browser verification.
- The game loop and dialog system must freeze simulation—not just animate under a visual overlay.
- The opening sequence should begin with Dad stationary in bed and the three girls walking into position before the wake-up dialog.
- The player must be able to exit the bedroom and cross all room door gaps using collision-aware movement.
- Dad loses if temper reaches zero and wins only after everyone, including Dad, is tucked in.

## Requirements
- Preserve keyboard/touch movement and collision-aware continuous movement.

- Keep gameplay paused by choice dialogs.

- Use target-based smooth movement rather than teleportation.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish and validate `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html` as a playable, tablet-friendly household RPG where Dad completes the household sequence and gets into bed.

## Requirements
- Preserve keyboard/touch controls, continuous collision-aware movement, real walls and passable door gaps, responsive tablet layout, and full-game pauses during choice dialogs.
- Keep chores in order: breakfast, showers, laundry, dishes, then tuck in Elaina, Elsie, and Ellerle.
- Dad’s bedtime is separate from the chore checklist and not delegable; Dad gets into bed himself after all girls are tucked in.
- Dad cannot move while in bed.
- Before gameplay begins, show an opening screen describing the objective and offering a “Start game” option.
- Keep breakfast at the shared dining table, with all three girls seated before completion and no visible “Breakfast” or “Dishes” labels on props.
- Preserve Charlie’s nap/trip/bark behavior, temporary character speech bubbles, cooperation/resistance, implicit dialogue choices, temper, focus, breaks, and win/loss conditions.
- NPC room-to-room movement must follow doorways and room paths rather than direct lines through walls.

## Decisions
- Use a single-page canvas game with an HTML sidebar and touch controls.
- Starting the game opens the introductory objective screen first; it must be dismissed with “Start game.”
- Dad remains non-awake and unable to move while in bed.
- The opening wake-up dialog uses “Get out of bed” as the action to begin Dad’s movement.
- Parenting approaches remain implicit through spoken commands, not named style categories.
- Bathroom/laundry, kitchen, hallway, bedrooms, and living room remain separate collision areas connected by actual gaps.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added the in-file opening/start screen with the game objective and “Start game” button.
- Added a `started` gate so gameplay timers, movement, and game progression remain inactive until the opening is dismissed.
- Changed Dad’s initial state so he stays in bed and cannot move before waking.
- Added “Get out of bed” as the opening wake-up action.
- Added one confirmed “five more minutes” path that later offers “Get out of bed” again.
- Previous core implementation work remains present: canvas house, chores, dialogs, Dad/girl/Charlie rendering, kitchen appliances/table, breakfast seating check, laundry timing, bedtime tasks, and Dad bed win interaction.
- JavaScript syntax validation previously passed with `new Function(js)`.

### Active

- **Let it wait briefly**
- **Take a break together**
- **Offer a choice**
- **Follow through consistently**

These choices affect the child immediately and change future behavior.

### Examples
- Calm requests work better with high-trust, already-cooperative children.
- Firm commands may be effective for older children but increase resistance in tired or sensitive younger children.
- Rewards work for younger children but lose effectiveness after repeated use.
- Helping the child start improves cooperation and trust.
- Hurried or repeated reminders can increase frustration.
- Consistent follow-through improves future compliance.
- Inconsistent commands or letting repeated resistance go increase future refusal.

### Midday schedule
- **Breakfast:** all three girls seated at the shared table.
- **Showers/getting ready:** characters can cooperate or need reminders.
- **Laundry:** Dad or a child starts and completes the task.
- **Lunch:** girls gather and sit at the table.
- **Dishes:** Dad or delegated children clear and wash dishes.
- **Afternoon activities:** reading, chores, play, and Charlie interactions.
- **Dinner:** all girls gather for dinner.
- **Bedtime:** each girl is tucked into their own bed.
- **Dad's bedtime:** available only after all girls are tucked in.

### Task assistance
Dad can use a command dialog near a child or a home station.

Possible options include:
- **Ask calmly**
- **Give a clear instruction**
- **Offer to help**
- **Offer a small reward**
- **Delegate this step**
- **Give a gentle reminder**
- **Say “Hurry up”**
- **Let them try independently**
- **Check back later**

The requested child can then:
- Cooperate immediately
- Cooperate after a reminder
- Resist
- Become distracted
- Delegate the task onward
- Ask Dad for help
- React using a temporary speech bubble

Repeated resistance pauses the task, lowers trust or temper, and opens more prompt options. It does not block progress forever.

### Task progress
A task will require both assignment and progress:
1. Dad interacts with a station or child.
2. Dad chooses a prompt.
3. The child accepts, resists, or delays.
4. An accepted child travels to the correct room using valid routes.
5. The child performs the task over time or assists Dad.
6. Progress appears in the checklist/sidebar.
7. A task is complete only when Dad or a cooperating child reaches the requirement.

### Future behavior examples
- If Dad calmly follows through repeatedly, a child becomes more responsive.
- If Dad uses only firm commands, resistance increases over time.
- If a child is rewarded repeatedly for the same task, the reward becomes less effective.
- If Dad delegates successfully to an older child, delegation becomes more effective for that child.
- Younger children may cooperate better with help and rewards.
- Older children may respond better to calm, choice-based, or responsibility-based approaches.
- Refusing a command after a prior successful pattern can trigger stronger temporary reactions.

### Pause behavior
Choice dialogs remain full-game freezes:
- Characters stop
- Routes stop
- Timers stop
- Laundry stops
- Meals do not progress
- Dad cannot move
- Charlie pauses
- Temper/focus timers pause
- The current prompt stays open until a choice is made

### Win/loss conditions
- Win by completing the full day and putting Dad in bed.
- Lose if Dad's temper reaches zero or the full day is not managed successfully.

Continue maintaining:
- Real walls and door gaps
- Collision-aware movement
- Continuous keyboard/touch movement
- Tablet-friendly layout
- Existing Charlie behavior
- Temporary speech bubbles
- Breakfast at the shared dining table
- Breakfast and dishes without visible labels on the props
- Dad as non-awake and immovable in bed until awakened
- Dad unavailable to move while a dialog is open or after winning

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and validate a single-page, tablet-friendly household RPG where Dad manages a full day and then gets into bed.

## Requirements
- Preserve keyboard/touch controls, continuous collision-aware movement, real walls and passable door gaps, and responsive tablet layout.
- Freeze timers and gameplay during choice dialogs.
- Dad starts in bed, must wake, cannot move while asleep or after winning, and wins only after all three girls are tucked in.
- Keep chores in order and expand the day to: breakfast, showers/getting ready, laundry, lunch, dishes, afternoon activities, dinner, then bedtime.
- Breakfast requires all three girls seated at the shared dining table; dishes and breakfast props have no visible labels.
- Kids may cooperate or resist based on mood and history; Dad needs practical commands and task delegation options.
- Parenting approaches affect immediate behavior and persist in future choices.
- Characters must use collision-aware doorway routing between rooms instead of direct paths through walls.
- Preserve Charlie's nap, trip, and living-room bark behavior.
- Dad's break, temper, focus, speech bubbles, win/loss conditions, and temporary messages remain required.

## Decisions
- Recommended full-day structure: breakfast → showers/getting ready → laundry → lunch → dishes → afternoon activities → dinner → tuck in Elaina/Elsie/Ellerle → Dad gets into bed.
- Parenting style names remain implicit; use spoken commands such as “Hurry up,” “Please come here,” and “Meet me at the table.”
- Choices must have lasting effects on trust, mood, cooperation, and resistance.
- NPC routing must follow a room graph and real doorway waypoints.
- Room routing has priority over direct destination movement.

## Work State
### Completed
- Opening/start screen and separate wake-up dialog were added.
- Dad initially has `awake: false` and is rendered immobile in bed.
- “Get out of bed” and the “five quiet minutes” wake path were implemented.
- Opening, dialogue, Dad movement, chore, bed, sidebar, touch, and canvas foundations are present.
- A room graph and waypoint helper were added to `index.html`.
- Dad-bed win interaction requires all three girls' bed tasks.
- JavaScript syntax validation previously passed with `new Function(js)`.

### Active
- Replace remaining direct-character movement with reliable doorway/room waypoint routing.
- Expand the checklist and schedule through lunch, afternoon activities, dinner, and bedtime.
- Add persistent kid mood, trust, help history, reward effectiveness, and resistance tracking.
- Add a routed “Hurry up” command and other spoken command prompts.
- Implement task assistance where a cooperating child travels to and performs an assigned task.
- Verify Charlie's routed nap, trip, and bark behavior.

### Blocked
- Interactive Chromium/Playwright browser verification remains unavailable.

## Next Move
1. Audit every girl and Charlie destination assignment in `step()` and `interact()` to ensure `setDestination()`/room waypoints are used.
2. Repair room graph doorway coordinates and ensure no character is routed through bedroom or hallway walls.
3. Replace any remaining direct movement toward kitchens, tables, beds, and outdoor/living-room locations.
4. Add command prompts, including “Hurry up,” with cooperation/resistance outcomes and temporary speech bubbles.
5. Implement persistent parenting consequences and a full-day task schedule.
6. Validate opening, waking, routing, chores, meal seating, dialogue pauses, bedtime, Charlie behavior, and Dad's bed win in a browser when available.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main implementation for canvas, routing, chores, NPC behavior, dialogs, controls, and UI.

## Important Context
- Dad's starting state depends on `player.awake`; it is `false` until “Get out of bed” is selected.
- `paused` freezes the whole game during dialogs; `started` separately gates pre-game behavior.
- `roomLinks`, `roomAt()`, `setDestination()`, and `moveActor()` are the routing symbols in `index.html`.
- Current reported defect: characters still attempt direct travel toward destinations such as the kitchen through walls.
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A browser route cannot be approved merely from source inspection; Chromium/Playwright verification remains pending.

- Complete and validate a tablet-friendly, single-page household RPG about Dad completing a full day and finally getting into bed.

## Requirements
- Preserve keyboard/touch controls, continuous collision-aware movement, real walls and passable door gaps, responsive tablet layout, and no scrolling in the sidebar.
- Freeze timers and gameplay during dialogs.
- Dad starts asleep in bed, must wake, cannot move asleep or after winning, and wins only after all three girls are tucked in and he gets into his own bed.

- Breakfast requires all three girls seated at the shared dining table; meal and dish props have no visible labels.
- Kids may cooperate or resist based on mood and history; Dad needs commands and delegation options.
- Parenting choices affect immediate behavior and persist in later choices.
- NPCs must use room graph doorway routing rather than direct paths through walls.
- Preserve Charlie’s nap, trip, living-room bark behavior, Dad’s break, temper, focus, speech bubbles, and win/loss conditions.

## Decisions
- Use implicit parenting styles through spoken commands such as “Hurry up,” “Please come here,” “Meet me at the table,” and practical delegations.
- Dialog choices persist in trust, mood, cooperation, and resistance.
- NPC routing prioritizes room graph links and real doorway waypoints.
- The sidebar must show all options and stats without scrolling, using compact and height-responsive styling.

### Completed
- Opening/start screen and separate wake-up dialog are implemented.
- Dad starts with `awake: false`, cannot move while asleep, and has get-out-of-bed and five-minutes wake paths.

## Objective
- Finish and balance the household RPG in `index.html`, preserving reliable chores and NPC behavior with responsive movement and mood interactions.

## Requirements
- Preserve daughter resistance/compliance rules based on mood, history, age, and parenting style.
- Keep meal, shower, laundry, task, and bedtime flows sequential and reliable.
- Grumpy girls move slowly; encouragement provides a temporary 1.65x speed boost.
- Refusal messages during chores must remain visible in the dialogue instead of being hidden or shaded behind the background.
- Add immediate, visible breakfast non-compliance with text bubbles above the girls’ heads.
- Charlie must roam all rooms, enter zoomies at roughly 2.8x speed, and bark once per newly visited room.
- Charlie proximity must show hearts and increase girls’ mood, compliance, and movement readiness.

## Decisions
- Reuse `calm`, `authoritarian`, `bribery`, and `delegate` parenting styles.
- Girl movement combines mood-based scaling with timed `encouragedLeft` encouragement.
- Charlie’s schedule includes naps, barking, patrols, and zoomies.
- Charlie routing uses room-aware `setDestination()` and `setMultiDestination()` routes.
- Refusal and breakfast-call responses should use visible dialogue/bubble content rather than background-shaded dialog states.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added mood-based girl movement penalties and mood-symbol behavior.
- Added encouragement/cheering boosts and nearby-girl prompt options.
- Added Charlie proximity hearts and nearby-girl mood/history boosts.
- Increased Charlie schedule variety and room patrol routing.
- Added Charlie zoomies, 2.8x zoomie movement, and per-room bark state.
- Added `routeBetween()` and `setMultiDestination()` room-aware routing.
- Fixed the broken `delegateTask` syntax.
- Added timed expiration for `encouragedLeft` and `heartLeft`.
- Inline JavaScript syntax validation passes.
- `git diff --check` passes.

### Active
- Implement and verify visible refusal bubbles within the active dialogue for showers and other chores.
- Implement immediate breakfast non-compliance and appropriate head bubbles for the girls.
- Browser gameplay validation remains pending for mood speed, cheering, hearts, patrols, zoomies, and doorway recovery.

### Blocked
- [none]

## Next Move
1. Adjust refusal handling so it updates the same visible dialogue and bubble state rather than opening content behind the shade.
2. Add breakfast-call resistance so the girls respond immediately with appropriate above-head text bubbles.
3. Test grumpy girls and confirm mood speed penalties are visible and reasonable.
4. Test cheering and prompt speed boosts and verify their timed expiration.

- Charlie proximity is handled at distance under 75 and sets `heartLeft=1.4`.
- `setDestination()` and `setMultiDestination()` support room-aware route generation.
- Inline JavaScript syntax and `git diff --check` have both passed.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Dad break reliability fix

Found two real reasons the break sometimes felt dead:

1. **While a dialog was open**, the dark dialog shade covered the whole screen, so the sidebar break button couldn't be clicked — even though it was right there. The break was only reachable between conversations.
2. **At 0 patience (game over)**, the button opened a dialog that restored patience but left `ended='lose'`, so nothing actually changed.

### Changes
- Added an **“☕ Take a dad break” choice to every dialog** (except the break dialog itself), so Dad can always step away mid-conversation. It only appears when a break is available.
- Added a **`B` keyboard shortcut** that opens the break from anywhere, including during a dialog.
- Added an `openDadBreak()` guard: on game over it now shows *“The day is already over—start a new day to try again.”* instead of a useless dialog; during cooldown it shows *“Dad needs Xs before another break.”*
- Removed the `disabled` attribute from the break button so clicks always give feedback (the countdown label still shows remaining time).
- Added `setBreak` to the debug hook for testing (consistent with the other setters).

- Full browser playtest: **passed** (all chores, Charlie, bedtime, win; no page/console errors).
- Mechanics test: **passed** (coffee, break recovery/cooldown, non-compliance pressure).
- Break diagnostic: confirmed break works during a dialog, via the B key, during cooldown (toast feedback), and at game over (clear message).
